title: How memories form and how we lose them - Catharine Young
speaker: TED-Ed
zh: 【TED-Ed】記憶是如何形成以及我們如何失去它們——凱瑟琳楊（精選雙語跟讀教材）

cues.text: Think back to a really vivid memory.
cues.en: Think back to a really vivid memory.
cues.zh: 試著回想你最鮮明的記憶。

cues.text: Got it?
cues.en: Got it?
cues.zh: 試著回想你最鮮明的記憶。 想到了嗎？ 好，回想三星期前你吃了什麼午餐。

cues.text: Okay, now try to remember what you had for lunch three weeks ago.
cues.en: Okay, now try to remember what you had for lunch three weeks ago.
cues.zh: 想到了嗎？ 好，回想三星期前你吃了什麼午餐。 第二個記憶可能沒第一個那麼強烈，

cues.text: That second memory probably isn't as strong, but why not?
cues.en: That second memory probably isn't as strong, but why not?
cues.zh: 第二個記憶可能沒第一個那麼強烈， 但為什麼呢？ 為什麼我們記得一些事， 卻忘了另一些呢？

cues.text: Why do we remember some things, and not others?
cues.en: Why do we remember some things, and not others?
cues.zh: 為什麼我們記得一些事， 卻忘了另一些呢？ 為什麼記憶最後會消逝呢？

cues.text: And why do memories eventually fade?
cues.en: And why do memories eventually fade?
cues.zh: 為什麼記憶最後會消逝呢？ 我們先看看最初記憶是如何成形的。

cues.text: Let's look at how memories form in the first place.
cues.en: Let's look at how memories form in the first place.
cues.zh: 我們先看看最初記憶是如何成形的。

cues.text: When you experience something, like dialing a phone number, the experience is converted into a pulse of electrical energy
cues.en: When you experience something, like dialing a phone number, the experience is converted into a pulse of electrical energy
cues.zh: 我們先看看最初記憶是如何成形的。 當你做某件事，如撥電話， 這經歷轉變成電脈衝能量 在神經元網路內流動。

cues.text: that zips along a network of neurons.
cues.en: that zips along a network of neurons.
cues.zh: 在神經元網路內流動。 訊息會先在短暫記憶區內停留，

cues.text: Information first lands in short term memory, where it's available from anywhere from a few seconds
cues.en: Information first lands in short term memory, where it's available from anywhere from a few seconds
cues.zh: 在神經元網路內流動。 訊息會先在短暫記憶區內停留， 停留數秒至數分鐘；

cues.text: to a couple of minutes.
cues.en: to a couple of minutes.
cues.zh: 停留數秒至數分鐘； 再經由如海馬迴這樣的區域 傳送到長期記憶區，

cues.text: It's then transferred to long-term memory through areas such as the hippocampus,
cues.en: It's then transferred to long-term memory through areas such as the hippocampus,
cues.zh: 再經由如海馬迴這樣的區域 傳送到長期記憶區， 最後到達腦內的數個儲存區域。

cues.text: and finally to several storage regions across the brain.
cues.en: and finally to several storage regions across the brain.
cues.zh: 最後到達腦內的數個儲存區域。

cues.text: Neurons throughout the brain communicate at dedicated sites called synapses
cues.en: Neurons throughout the brain communicate at dedicated sites called synapses
cues.zh: 最後到達腦內的數個儲存區域。 腦內各處的神經元 透過稱為突觸的特定地點

cues.text: using specialized neurotransmitters.
cues.en: using specialized neurotransmitters.
cues.zh: 透過稱為突觸的特定地點 利用專門的神經遞質彼此聯絡。

cues.text: If two neurons communicate repeatedly, a remarkable thing happens:
cues.en: If two neurons communicate repeatedly, a remarkable thing happens:
cues.zh: 利用專門的神經遞質彼此聯絡。 如果一對神經元重覆互聯， 就會有精彩的結果：

cues.text: the efficiency of communication between them increases.
cues.en: the efficiency of communication between them increases.
cues.zh: 它們之間的通訊效率提升。

cues.text: This process, called long term potentiation, is considered to be a mechanism by which memories are stored long-term,
cues.en: This process, called long term potentiation, is considered to be a mechanism by which memories are stored long-term,
cues.zh: 它們之間的通訊效率提升。 這個流程稱為長期增強作用， 被視為是長期記憶的儲存機制。

cues.text: but how do some memories get lost?
cues.en: but how do some memories get lost?
cues.zh: 被視為是長期記憶的儲存機制。 但是，為何有些記憶消逝了呢？

cues.text: Age is one factor.
cues.en: Age is one factor.
cues.zh: 老化是一個因素。

cues.text: As we get older, synapses begin to falter and weaken,
cues.en: As we get older, synapses begin to falter and weaken,
cues.zh: 隨著年長，突觸開始萎縮變弱，

cues.text: affecting how easily we can retrieve memories.
cues.en: affecting how easily we can retrieve memories.
cues.zh: 隨著年長，突觸開始萎縮變弱， 增加喚醒記憶的難度。

cues.text: Scientists have several theories about what's behind this deterioration,
cues.en: Scientists have several theories about what's behind this deterioration,
cues.zh: 科學家有數個腦退化原因的理論： 自腦部萎縮－

cues.text: from actual brain shrinkage, the hippocampus loses 5% of its neurons every decade
cues.en: from actual brain shrinkage, the hippocampus loses 5% of its neurons every decade
cues.zh: 科學家有數個腦退化原因的理論： 自腦部萎縮－ 海馬迴每十年損失5%的神經元，

cues.text: for a total loss of 20% by the time you're 80 years old
cues.en: for a total loss of 20% by the time you're 80 years old
cues.zh: 海馬迴每十年損失5%的神經元， 到80歲時，總共損失20%；

cues.text: to the drop in the production of neurotransmitters, like acetylcholine, which is vital to learning and memory.
cues.en: to the drop in the production of neurotransmitters, like acetylcholine, which is vital to learning and memory.
cues.zh: 至神經傳遞質的產出減少－ 像是乙醯膽鹼 這種學習和記憶不可或缺的元素。 這個變化似乎影響人們 喚醒儲存訊息的效率。

cues.text: These changes seem to affect how people retrieve stored information.
cues.en: These changes seem to affect how people retrieve stored information.
cues.zh: 這個變化似乎影響人們 喚醒儲存訊息的效率。

cues.text: Age also affects our memory-making abilities.
cues.en: Age also affects our memory-making abilities.
cues.zh: 這個變化似乎影響人們 喚醒儲存訊息的效率。 老化也降低記憶形成的能力。

cues.text: Memories are encoded most strongly when we're paying attention,
cues.en: Memories are encoded most strongly when we're paying attention,
cues.zh: 老化也降低記憶形成的能力。 最強的記憶編碼發生在我們留意，

cues.text: when we're deeply engaged, and when information is meaningful to us.
cues.en: when we're deeply engaged, and when information is meaningful to us.
cues.zh: 最強的記憶編碼發生在我們留意， 被深深地吸引， 和訊息對我們有意義時。

cues.text: Mental and physical health problems, which tend to increase as we age,
cues.en: Mental and physical health problems, which tend to increase as we age,
cues.zh: 被深深地吸引， 和訊息對我們有意義時。 隨著老化，增多的身心健康問題

cues.text: interfere with our ability to pay attention, and thus act as memory thieves.
cues.en: interfere with our ability to pay attention, and thus act as memory thieves.
cues.zh: 會干擾專注的能力， 就像盜走記憶的小偷。 另一個記憶問題的主因是長期壓力。

cues.text: Another leading cause of memory problems is chronic stress.
cues.en: Another leading cause of memory problems is chronic stress.
cues.zh: 另一個記憶問題的主因是長期壓力。 當我們於公、於私 持續背負重責和工作量時，

cues.text: When we're constantly overloaded with work and personal responsibilites,
cues.en: When we're constantly overloaded with work and personal responsibilites,
cues.zh: 當我們於公、於私 持續背負重責和工作量時，

cues.text: our bodies are on hyperalert.
cues.en: our bodies are on hyperalert.
cues.zh: 當我們於公、於私 持續背負重責和工作量時， 身體處於非常警覺狀態。

cues.text: This response has evolved from the physiological mechanism designed to make sure we can survive in a crisis.
cues.en: This response has evolved from the physiological mechanism designed to make sure we can survive in a crisis.
cues.zh: 身體處於非常警覺狀態。 這是心理機制進化的反應， 目的是使我們能夠 應付危機，生存下來。

cues.text: Stress chemicals help mobilize energy and increase alertness.
cues.en: Stress chemicals help mobilize energy and increase alertness.
cues.zh: 目的是使我們能夠 應付危機，生存下來。 壓力化學物質有助 調動能量和增加警覺性。

cues.text: However, with chronic stress our bodies become flooded with these chemicals,
cues.en: However, with chronic stress our bodies become flooded with these chemicals,
cues.zh: 壓力化學物質有助 調動能量和增加警覺性。 但是，身體會因為長期壓力 而充滿這些化學物質，

cues.text: resulting in a loss of brain cells and an inability to form new ones,
cues.en: resulting in a loss of brain cells and an inability to form new ones,
cues.zh: 導致損失且無法新生腦細胞， 進一步影響保有記憶的能力。

cues.text: which affects our ability to retain new information.
cues.en: which affects our ability to retain new information.
cues.zh: 進一步影響保有記憶的能力。 憂鬱是另一個罪魁禍首。

cues.text: Depression is another culprit.
cues.en: Depression is another culprit.
cues.zh: 憂鬱是另一個罪魁禍首。 憂鬱的人生出記憶問題的機率 比一般人高出40%。

cues.text: People who are depressed are 40% more likely to develop memory problems.
cues.en: People who are depressed are 40% more likely to develop memory problems.
cues.zh: 憂鬱的人生出記憶問題的機率 比一般人高出40%。

cues.text: Low levels of serotonin, a neurotransmitter connected to arousal,
cues.en: Low levels of serotonin, a neurotransmitter connected to arousal,
cues.zh: 連線覺醒的神經傳遞質－ 血清素－含量過低， 可能使憂鬱的人較不留心新訊息。

cues.text: may make depressed individuals less attentive to new information.
cues.en: may make depressed individuals less attentive to new information.
cues.zh: 可能使憂鬱的人較不留心新訊息。 另一個憂鬱的症狀 是沉浸在過去的悲傷事件中，

cues.text: Dwelling on sad events in the past, another symptom of depression,
cues.en: Dwelling on sad events in the past, another symptom of depression,
cues.zh: 可能使憂鬱的人較不留心新訊息。 另一個憂鬱的症狀 是沉浸在過去的悲傷事件中，

cues.text: makes it difficult to pay attention to the present, affecting the ability to store short-term memories.
cues.en: makes it difficult to pay attention to the present, affecting the ability to store short-term memories.
cues.zh: 另一個憂鬱的症狀 是沉浸在過去的悲傷事件中， 難以對眼前的事物感興趣， 因此影響短期記憶的儲存能力。

cues.text: Isolation, which is tied to depression, is another memory thief.
cues.en: Isolation, which is tied to depression, is another memory thief.
cues.zh: 跟憂鬱緊緊相關的孤立 是另一個竊取記憶的賊。 哈佛大學公共健康部的研究發現

cues.text: A study by the Harvard School of Public Health found that older people with high levels of social integration
cues.en: A study by the Harvard School of Public Health found that older people with high levels of social integration
cues.zh: 跟憂鬱緊緊相關的孤立 是另一個竊取記憶的賊。 哈佛大學公共健康部的研究發現 與社會互動較多的長者，

cues.text: had a slower rate of memory decline over a six-year period.
cues.en: had a slower rate of memory decline over a six-year period.
cues.zh: 與社會互動較多的長者， 在六年間的記憶退化較緩慢。

cues.text: The exact reason remains unclear, but experts suspect that
cues.en: The exact reason remains unclear, but experts suspect that
cues.zh: 雖然還不清楚確切的原因， 但是專家推測 社會互動會活動大腦。

cues.text: social interaction gives our brain a mental workout.
cues.en: social interaction gives our brain a mental workout.
cues.zh: 社會互動會活動大腦。 就像肌肉強度，

cues.text: Just like muscle strength, we have to use our brain or risk losing it.
cues.en: Just like muscle strength, we have to use our brain or risk losing it.
cues.zh: 就像肌肉強度， 我們必須用腦，否則它就會退化。 但是不要絕望。

cues.text: But don't despair.
cues.en: But don't despair.
cues.zh: 我們必須用腦，否則它就會退化。 但是不要絕望。 有幾個可採取的步驟

cues.text: There are several steps you can take to aid your brain in preserving your memories.
cues.en: There are several steps you can take to aid your brain in preserving your memories.
cues.zh: 有幾個可採取的步驟 可以幫助大腦保持記憶。 一定要活絡筋骨－

cues.text: Make sure you keep physically active.
cues.en: Make sure you keep physically active.
cues.zh: 一定要活絡筋骨－ 增加血液流動到大腦是有益的。

cues.text: Increased blood flow to the brain is helpful.
cues.en: Increased blood flow to the brain is helpful.
cues.zh: 增加血液流動到大腦是有益的。 均衡飲食－

cues.text: And eat well.
cues.en: And eat well.
cues.zh: 增加血液流動到大腦是有益的。 均衡飲食－ 大腦需要有所有的好營養 才能正常運作。

cues.text: Your brain needs all the right nutrients to keep functioning correctly.
cues.en: Your brain needs all the right nutrients to keep functioning correctly.
cues.zh: 大腦需要有所有的好營養 才能正常運作。

cues.text: And finally, give your brain a workout.
cues.en: And finally, give your brain a workout.
cues.zh: 大腦需要有所有的好營養 才能正常運作。 最後，動動腦－

cues.text: Exposing your brain to challenges, like learning a new language, is one of the best defenses for keeping your memories intact.
cues.en: Exposing your brain to challenges, like learning a new language, is one of the best defenses for keeping your memories intact.
cues.zh: 最後，動動腦－ 給大腦一些挑戰，例如 學習新語言是保衛記憶完整 的最好方式之一。
